data.body:
AC2 EVIDENCE (part 2 of 2) — the per-class env-var invocations and the local-server recipe.

THIS IS THE PART THAT FOUND A REAL DEFECT, so it is recorded before the pass/fail summary.

--- WHAT EXECUTING THE COMMANDS REVEALED ---
The section's three examples all read `… rebar review <id>`. Executed as written:
    $ REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o rebar review 8625-7bea-67db-4cdc -o json
    -> ran, but on "model": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8", and stamped
       provider_provenance {provider: bedrock, tier: first_class}
i.e. the documented command did NOT produce the documented result. Diagnosed rather than assumed:
  * `resolve_model(cfg, step, workflow)` returns `resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model)`
    (config.py:297). `rebar review` supplies neither a step nor a workflow class, so it resolves
    `cfg.model` — this project's `[tool.rebar.llm].model` Bedrock pin — and a class slot is never
    consulted.
  * I first hypothesised the top-level pin was merely SHADOWING the class. That was WRONG and a
    control refuted it: in a scratch repo with NO top-level `model`, `resolve_model(cfg)` returned
    the DEFAULT (`claude-opus-4-8`), still not `openai:gpt-4o`. The class is not shadowed; it is
    not consulted at all by a classless operation.
  * A narrow grep then suggested `frontier` had NO consumer anywhere. Searching ALL file types
    corrected that: `gates/code-review.yaml:74` declares `model: frontier` (and `:174`, `:209`
    declare `model: standard`), so the class IS live — through workflow STEP declarations, not
    through a Python `FRONTIER_CLASS` constant.
The mechanism the prose claims ("the same slots are settable from the environment") is therefore
TRUE; only the example commands were wrong. MEASURED:
    resolve_model(cfg)                  -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8  (what `rebar review` uses)
    resolve_model(cfg, step='frontier') -> openai:gpt-4o
    resolve_model(cfg, step='standard') -> google:gemini-2.5-pro
FIXED in Gerrit change 1350, MERGED as 996a3b107f: each example now names an operation that
actually declares the class it sets, plus an explicit statement of the shadowing rule and the
measurement behind it.

--- THE CORRECTED COMMANDS, EXECUTED ---
1. frontier — END TO END, live:
     $ REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW=1 REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o \
         rebar review-code --base origin/main --head HEAD
     -> llm call [code-review-base] mode=agentic model=openai:gpt-4o FAILED in 4.4s:
        status_code: 429 … 'credit_balance_exhausted'
   The Pass-1 finder step was routed to `openai:gpt-4o` and the request REACHED OpenAI's API; the
   only failure is that this account has no credits — an account billing state, not a routing
   failure. This is the affirmative proof that `rebar review-code` DOES honour
   REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL where `rebar review` does not, i.e. that the correction is right.
   (`rebar review-code` is off by default locally — `verify.enable_code_review: false` — hence the
   documented-elsewhere REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW override; without it the command returns
   "code-review capability disabled".)
2. standard — routing proven by resolution (above): step='standard' -> google:gemini-2.5-pro.
   NOT run end to end, and the reason is itself the documented behaviour: `pydantic-ai-slim[google]`
   is not installed here, and attempting the Google provider raises exactly the error the section
   promises — "Please install the `google-genai` package … you can use the `google` optional
   group". Installing it was declined deliberately: the only venv available was the one the full
   suite was running in.
3. trivial / local OpenAI-compatible server — EXECUTED against a real endpoint. See the epic
   comment for the full four-assertion probe; in summary the composition
   REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL + REBAR_LLM_API_KEY + REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai built a provider that
   `isinstance(..., OpenAIProvider)` is True for, with base_url = the local endpoint and
   provenance tier `best_effort`, and a REAL request was served
   (`STUB_RECEIVED path=/v1/chat/completions model=local-model auth=True`). Also exercised against
   the LMStudio instance running on this host's :1234 — a genuine third-party OpenAI-compatible
   server — which returned a real OpenAI-shaped response, proving the routing independently.
   The claim "no dummy REBAR_LLM_API_KEY needed — the builder supplies one" and the
   `tier=best_effort` claim both hold.

--- AC1 and AC3, verified line-by-line against the MERGED text (not by inspection of intent) ---
AC1: docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md on origin/main, 992 lines,
     "**Status:** Accepted". Its "## Alternatives rejected" section names ALL FIVE required
     alternatives, each with its rejecting evidence:
       LiteLLM in-process (line 672 — and honest about it: it explicitly declines to repeat the
         epic's uncited "documented to drift" phrase as fact, resting on the OpenHands
         `model_features.py` observation instead)
       a gateway fronting Bedrock (689)
       REFUSING to sign off-tier verdicts (730)
       a long-term Bedrock API key in SSM (738)
       a cross-provider FallbackModel to direct Anthropic (753)
     plus four more it was not required to cover (elif chain, per-call-site force_prompted,
     profile-flags-only capability rule, provider.startswith prefix matching, gateway stamped
     first_class).
AC3: docs/llm-framework.md §"Provider support tiers" states, per tier, what is GUARANTEED —
     first_class: "native rebar builder, capabilities derived from the real ModelProfile, covered
     by the unit suite and the provider-parity harness"; best_effort: "an intermediary may have
     rewritten the request; rebar cannot vouch for what reached the model" — and what a consumer
     may INFER, as three named limits: the tier is a CONFIGURATION-TIME fact and does not prove
     where traffic went; it lives in the sidecar and is NOT part of the signed bytes; and
     first_class does NOT currently imply retry/timeout parity (REBAR_LLM_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS /
     REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT reach the Anthropic path only).

--- AC4 ---
     $ python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check   -> EXIT 0
   Confirmed by exit code on three separate clean trees this session (129e, 8625, 846b worktrees).
   Re-running the generator left `git status --porcelain` EMPTY, so docs/env-vars.md is current and
   legitimately untouched by this change: the change adds no new env-var READ in Python.
